transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I have this intense, overwhelming fear of dogs that I just can't manage on my own anymore. It's gotten to the point where it feels completely out of control, and I really need some help.
What happens when you see a dog or are in a situation where you might encounter a dog?

Even just thinking about the possibility of running into a dog triggers intense anxiety for me. If I actually see one, I instantly panic—my heart races, I start sweating and shaking, and I feel completely frozen and unable to move.
Is your fear limited to dogs, or are there other animals or situations that also trigger this kind of anxiety response in you?

No, it's actually not just dogs. I get that same terrifying panic with other things like spiders, heights, storms, seeing blood, and enclosed spaces like elevators. I even have an intense fear of choking or loud, sudden sounds.
How long have you been experiencing these fears, and have they always been present or did they start at some point in your life?
I've been experiencing these intense fears for about a year and ten months now. They haven't always been present; they actually started around that time and have been a constant struggle ever since.
Have these fears and anxieties significantly impacted your daily life, such as interfering with your work, relationships, or social activities?

Yes, they have severely impacted my life. I've had to accept major restrictions on my daily routines, social activities, and even my work just to make sure I completely avoid encountering any of my triggers.
Do you experience any recurring, intrusive thoughts or feel compelled to perform specific rituals or behaviors in response to your fears or anxieties?

No, I don't experience those kinds of recurring intrusive thoughts, nor do I feel compelled to perform any specific rituals or behaviors. My anxiety is really just focused on the intense fear and trying to avoid the things I'm afraid of.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about everyday things, even when there's no apparent reason to worry, or is your anxiety primarily focused on the specific phobias you've mentioned?
No, I don't worry excessively about everyday things. My anxiety is strictly focused on my specific phobias and the intense dread of potentially encountering those triggers.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by your anxiety being strictly focused on your specific phobias, and if there are any situations or times when you feel anxious without an obvious trigger?

I only feel anxious when I am directly facing one of my fears, or when I'm anticipating that I might run into them. I never experience anxiety out of the blue or without a specific trigger. It is always tied directly to those objects or situations.
